steps: Stop Core/worker after checking that no runtime/build/database jobs are active; preserve any later user writes and take a fresh scoped backup.

Review the guarded rollback frame SQL against the current mapping snapshot. It reattaches the same original installations and revokes frame credentials; the new addresses remain reserved. A changed mapping causes refusal. Do not restore the entire old Core dump over later user data.

Restore the original four settings files, addresses.json and Nginx copies from the private backup; do not overwrite credentials.json or init.sql. Apply the recorded identity-revert-plan.json PUTs using the loopback admin endpoint.

Recreate only Keycloak with the recorded compose-keycloak-rollback.json and old compose.env; preserve its exact image, network, mount and limits. Restore the saved 9443 redirect, validate Nginx and reload.

Start the previously running app containers and Core/worker with matching old origins. Recreate the same pilot image through the old console API if its stored Core origin must be reverted, then restore its stopped state. Verify old OIDC, health, CLI/MCP, mappings and app DB preservation.
